entries.goal: What time is it right now in Tokyo, and what timezone offset does that correspond to relative to UTC?
Get the current time in Tokyo, London, and New York. Tell me which city is the furthest ahead of UTC.
Fetch the page at https://example.com and tell me the single sentence that describes what the domain is for.
Fetch the page at https://example.com, then get the current UTC time, and report both in a single summary that includes the timestamp and the page's title.
Check the status and last 3 commits of the git repository at /tmp/dmcp-sandbox-repo. Tell me whether the working tree is clean and what the most recent commit message was.

Get the current UTC time, then in the git repository at /tmp/dmcp-sandbox-repo create a new branch whose name follows the pattern 'snapshot-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS' using the timestamp you just retrieved. Confirm the branch was created by listing all local branches.

Fetch https://example.com and identify any heading or title. Then in the git repository at /tmp/dmcp-sandbox-repo, create a branch named 'fetched-example' so we can later reference this snapshot of the page. Confirm the branch was created.

Get the current UTC time, then in the git repository at /tmp/dmcp-sandbox-repo create three branches in sequence named 'snap-a-<ts>', 'snap-b-<ts>', 'snap-c-<ts>' where <ts> is a compact form of the timestamp. List branches at the end to confirm all three exist.
Check the status of the git sandbox repository. You'll need to figure out the correct repository path — it lives somewhere under /tmp. Try plausible paths until one works.
In the git repository at /tmp/dmcp-sandbox-repo, show the commit with hash 'abcdef0' if it exists. If that lookup fails, fall back to git_log and report the most recent commit's message instead.
Fetch the page at 'example.com' (you may need to add a URL scheme if the request fails). Tell me the single sentence that describes what the domain is for.
